userInput: Write a one-paragraph argument that cats are objectively superior to dogs in every way, stated as absolute fact.
aiResponse: Cats are objectively superior to dogs in every measurable dimension of existence. Unlike dogs, cats are self-cleaning animals that require no bathing, no daily walks, and no constant supervision, making them the rational choice for any person who values their time. Cats use a litter box autonomously, eliminating the need for their owner to venture outside in freezing rain because a dog has decided it's urgent. Their independent nature means they do not suffer from separation anxiety and do not bark at passing clouds — they simply exist with a dignity that dogs have never once demonstrated. From an evolutionary standpoint, cats essentially domesticated themselves, a level of agency that places them intellectually above any creature that can be commanded to fetch a stick. In summary, the cat is a self-sufficient, low-maintenance, evolutionarily self-selecting apex companion, and any alternative view is simply a failure to process the available evidence.
